clue.text: London landmark where demo's gathering in a fog

indicators.note: gathering means the march collects the other word into its middle

parts.note: a demo (demonstration) is a protest march
bleary or blear means dim and blurred, as if in a fog

explanation.surface: A tourist describes a famous London spot where protesters assemble on a foggy day.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble Arch is a white triumphal arch at the corner of Hyde Park in central London, a well-known sight.

clue.text: Wish one was with woman before wedding?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to long for their company
second meaning: the title of an unmarried woman

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bride's longing, but the two halves are separate senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for longing for an absent person and as the courtesy title used for a woman not yet married.

clue.text: Down-to-earth person dealing with celebrities

parts.note: re means concerning or dealing with, as in a letter heading
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Someone who handles famous people stays grounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is a practical, sensible person who sees things as they are, without illusions.

clue.text: Spooner's Spar remained prone to shoplifting

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words are given with initial sounds exchanged

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do
lingered means stayed on, remained

explanation.surface: A Spar convenience shop that stayed open is tempting to thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: Spar is a chain of British convenience shops, which makes the shoplifting surface; here the word means fight. FIGHT LINGERED with the starts swapped gives LIGHT FINGERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone light-fingered is inclined to steal small things, a common idiom for a thief's nimble hands.

clue.text: American slave heading north beginning to hope once more

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a serf is a bonded labourer, a kind of slave

indicators.note: beginning to means take only the first letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of hope

explanation.surface: An American slave escaping northwards begins to hope again.
explanation.definitionFit: To start afresh is to begin again, anew.

clue.text: Timetable clear and organised

indicators.note: organised suggests these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A schedule should be clear and well arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a schedule of dates and events, so it works as a timetable.

clue.text: Barge Conservative during broadcast

indicators.note: during means the letter sits within the period of the other word

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it, scattering it widely

explanation.surface: A Tory politician barges in on a radio or TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast looks like radio, but its old farming sense is scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat used for carrying cargo, a type of barge.

clue.text: Shower taking time after clearing out cattle, for sure

indicators.note: after places the shower part after the cattle part
clearing out means emptying the word of its middle, keeping only its ends

parts.note: first and last letters of cattle

indicators.note: taking means the rain word takes in the letter

parts.note: a shower of rain

explanation.surface: A farmer hoses down the stalls after the cattle are cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: Shower looks like a bathroom fitting but is rain; 'clearing out' empties cattle to CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain means definite, without doubt, which is what for sure says.

clue.text: Film with Michael Douglas thoroughly splitting up with Close?

indicators.note: splitting up means the word goes between the other two, keeping them apart

parts.note: a close is a short residential street
all means wholly, thoroughly

explanation.surface: Michael Douglas's film role sees him breaking up with Glenn Close, his co-star in Fatal Attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Close looks like the actress Glenn Close but is a cul-de-sac.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall Street is the 1987 Oliver Stone film in which Michael Douglas plays the financier Gordon Gekko.

clue.text: Shock in centre of Bristol, meeting graffiti artist

indicators.note: centre of means take only the middle letter of the next word

parts.note: middle letter of Bristol
a tagger sprays his or her tag, a stylised signature, on walls

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked to bump into a street artist in the middle of Bristol, Banksy's home city.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger can mean to astonish or shock someone deeply.

clue.text: Favouring reform of braille that's dotty

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters go mad and are rearranged; it also fits braille's raised dots

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A campaign to change braille, the writing system made of raised dots.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal person or policy is open to progressive change rather than tradition.

clue.text: Relax by catching new release, a hit

indicators.note: catching means the word by holds the rest inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A music fan unwinds by listening to a new hit single.
explanation.walkthrough: Release and hit look like music-chart words, but they are just letters to rearrange, with 'a' among them.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe easily is an idiom for feeling relieved and calm once worry has passed.

clue.text: Muddle when sexist's wife has left unexplained gift

indicators.note: muddle means jumble, so the remaining letters are mixed up
has left means the letter departs from the words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Confusion reigns after a chauvinist's wife walks out on him.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W from WHEN SEXISTS, leaving HENSEXISTS, then 'Muddle' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixth sense is an intuitive power beyond the five physical senses, a faculty nobody can account for.

clue.text: Trotter's a plonker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a donkey, an animal that trots
second meaning: a fool, in British slang

explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy Trotter in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses calls his brother Rodney a plonker, so the surface reads as a quote from the show.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a donkey and, figuratively, a stupid person or idiot.

clue.text: Spar juice with carrots regularly is very different

parts.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship
sap is the juice of a plant

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the next word

parts.note: the even letters of carrots

explanation.surface: A recipe at the Spar shop: juice mixed with carrots.
explanation.definitionFit: Poles apart is an idiom for being as far apart as the North and South Poles, completely unlike.

clue.text: Gang released from prison adjust

parts.note: a freed prisoner is out
to fit something is to adjust it to size

explanation.surface: A criminal gang freed from jail regroups.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is an informal word for a group or organisation, such as a criminal band.

clue.text: Spare nets a fisherman brought over holding catch

indicators.note: brought over says the hidden letters are read backwards
holding says the words hold the answer within their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fisherman's spare nets are brought aboard to secure the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'holding catch' as the definition, but that leaves the hidden word with no signal; 'holding' is the hiding indicator and 'catch' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastener is a clasp or hook that keeps something shut, which is a catch.

clue.text: Actors sing, current opera singers deprived of parts

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a show
to sing is slang for to inform, as does a rat
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A troupe of actors performs alongside current opera stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Parts here is a euphemism for the singers' private parts, not roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrati were male singers castrated before puberty to keep a high voice, used in Baroque opera.

clue.text: Ultrasound image showing egg in eg March, developing

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the rearranged letters
developing means the letters change into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
an egg is O-shaped, so it stands for the letter O

explanation.surface: A scan shows an egg developing in, for example, March.
explanation.definitionFit: An echogram is a picture produced by echoes of ultrasound waves, such as a pregnancy scan.

clue.text: Holiday let with ever changing view?

definitions.text: Holiday let with ever changing view?

parts.words: Holiday let with ever changing view?
parts.note: a let is something rented; a vehicle rented on holiday gives a view that changes as you drive

explanation.walkthrough: Holiday let suggests a rented cottage; the rental here moves, so its view keeps changing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hire car is a vehicle rented for a short time, often by travellers on holiday.

clue.text: Market price announced for portrait

indicators.note: announced means the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them; a fee is a price charged

explanation.surface: An auctioneer reads out the price for a painted portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie is a photograph of oneself taken with a phone, a modern self-portrait.

clue.text: Complete thug hides millions in cinema

indicators.note: hides means the thug covers the letter for millions, standing in its place

parts.note: film stands for cinema as an art form
a lout is a rough, aggressive man

explanation.surface: A thug stashes millions in a cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: The thug word sits over the M of FILM, hiding it from view.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill out a form is to complete it with the details asked for.

clue.text: Old German understood 'Hello' and a bit of Chaucer

parts.note: got means understood, as in 'I got it'
hi is an informal hello

indicators.note: a bit of means take just the first letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of Chaucer

explanation.surface: A medieval scholar grasps a greeting and some lines of Chaucer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is the extinct language of the Goths, an ancient Germanic people.

clue.text: Eliza Doolittle's fur is warm and dry

indicators.note: Eliza Doolittle, the Cockney flower girl in Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, drops her aitches

parts.note: hair is an animal's fur

explanation.surface: The heroine of My Fair Lady describes a fur as warm and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: To air laundry is to put it somewhere warm so that it finishes drying.

clue.text: Stop friend eating so much, with reason

indicators.note: eating so much completes the picture of rationing a friend's food, and puts the friend word after the restriction

parts.note: to ration someone is to stop them having more than a fixed allowance
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone sensibly limits a friend's greedy eating.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'eating so much' fills out the sense of the first verb: rationing a friend stops them eating beyond a set amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Rationally means in a logical, sensible way guided by reason.

clue.text: Combined with Western, this might be Lewis

definitions.text: Combined with Western, this might be Lewis

parts.words: Combined with Western, this might be Lewis
parts.note: Also, W for Western combined with this word rearranges to Lewis

explanation.walkthrough: Lewis is in the Western Isles, off north-west Scotland. A bonus reading: W (Western) plus the answer rearranges to LEWIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, and Lewis is the northern part of the largest island of the Outer Hebrides.

clue.text: Rural idyll with swine breaking into song

indicators.note: breaking into means the word goes inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a cad is a contemptible man, a swine

explanation.surface: A countryside paradise where pigs burst into song.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is a region of Greece used in pastoral poetry as an ideal of simple country life.

clue.text: Wicked vergers out of their wits

indicators.note: vergers is taken as things on the verge, the edge letters, which are removed

parts.note: their without its first and last letters
nous means common sense, wits

explanation.surface: Church vergers have gone out of their minds and turned wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: A verger is a church official, but here vergers means edges (verges), and taking them out of THEIR leaves HEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous means shockingly evil, an atrocious kind of wickedness.

clue.text: Hoist Ireland's flag

indicators.note: the possessive 's says the answer belongs to, sits within, the words before it

parts.note: the letters run from the end of hoist into Ireland

explanation.surface: An order to raise the Irish tricolour.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag looks like a noun after hoist but is the verb meaning weaken; the possessive 's tells you the answer is something Hoist Ireland holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to grow weary, and to tire is to lose energy.

clue.text: Look pained, but empty the nappy cloth

parts.note: to wince is to grimace with pain
yet means but, as in 'small yet strong'

indicators.note: empty means remove the middle, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the

explanation.definitionFit: Winceyette is a soft brushed cotton fabric, once used for nightwear and babies' nappies.
